hypothesis: Current-season opponent-adjusted offense and prevention ratings with partial pooling reduce margin/total forecast error relative to symmetric current-season PF/PA averages.
inputs: Public nflverse regular-season games, 2016–2025; current-season completed games only for team ratings. Both teams require three prior completed games. Whole weekly folds; scores available conservatively kickoff+12h before first fold kickoff.
formula: score(team, opponent) = current league mean + venue/2 + ridge offense(team) + ridge allowed(opponent). Venue is current observed home margin shrunk by 64 games; offense/defense zero-centered with a three-game zero prior, 24 fixed coordinate updates.
coefficient_tuning: None. Alpha=3, venue prior=64 and 24 iterations fixed before run. No recency/efficiency/weather/injury coefficients invented.
holdout_warning: 2024–25 outcomes have been used in previous unrelated audits. This is a locked retrospective comparison, not a pristine untouched promotion holdout. Sealed prospective 2026 Week6 onward is required before production probability promotion; no Week5 ABBEYS holdout scoring.
comparators: Actual public closing total/spread only as a diagnostic benchmark, not executable decision-time quote
metrics: season-week cluster bootstrap paired improvement 95% CI
80% prediction interval coverage using 2016–22 out-of-sample residual quantiles
acceptance: Research contender only if held retrospective MAE improvement >=0.25 points and paired 95% lower bound >0, no season MAE deterioration >0.25, and interval coverage within 75–85%. Failure is retained/reported; production stays unchanged. Markets evaluated independently.
scope: First bounded game-score challenger within all-market opportunity/efficiency rebuild. Player markets have separate targets, distributions and data gates. A model lean does not need to outperform the closing line; confidence must be supported by calibrated error.
